comparison: Perfect alignment on background and motivation claims (C1-C3, C8-C13). Both evaluations find these claims well-supported by appropriate citations to prior work. OpenEval emphasizes accurate representation of the field, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the problem statement as valid.

Strong agreement on rank-1 model findings (C4, C21-C28). Both evaluations support that rank-1 networks can only implement input modulation. OpenEval includes additional claims about irrelevant information persistence (C29-C30) not explicitly addressed in peer review. All reviewers describe results as 'convincing.'

Agreement on rank-3 model capabilities (C32, C34-C38). Both evaluations confirm higher-rank networks are required for selection vector modulation. OpenEval additionally addresses indistinguishability from rank-1 models (C39-C40) and includes C5, which peer review groups separately. Both find results convincing.

Both address the link between intermediate variables and context-dependent modulation (C42). OpenEval includes C6 and C41 as part of information flow analysis. Peer review emphasizes this as a key contribution addressing an open question, with C15 also included. Both evaluations are strongly supportive.

Perfect agreement on pathway-based framework equivalence (C47-C48). Both evaluations support the theoretical and numerical validation. Peer reviewers praise the 'impressive' analytic approach, while OpenEval emphasizes validation across parameter regimes.

Complete alignment on geometric understanding of intermediate variables and contextual modulation (C49-C51). Peer review explicitly notes 'very clear identification of mechanisms,' while OpenEval emphasizes the logical connection established through the pathway-based framework.

Perfect agreement on correlation between network dimensionality and modulation mechanism (C52-C54). Both evaluations highlight the surprising strength of this result. Peer review emphasizes the difficulty of differentiating mechanisms, making the high correlation particularly notable.

Strong agreement on response kernel analysis findings (C55-C59). Both evaluations support that intermediate profiles indicate extra dimensions. OpenEval includes C7 as well. Peer review describes these as 'novel neural dynamical signatures' that are convincing.

Complete alignment on PEV-based index for quantifying selection vector modulation (C60-C62). Both evaluations support the SVD analysis and correlation findings. Peer review explicitly highlights this as a 'promising future avenue' for neural recordings.

Agreement on methodological advantages of low-rank RNN approach (C14-C15, C63). Peer review praises the 'impressive' analytic approach and 'important set of analyses,' while OpenEval emphasizes consistency with low-rank RNN theory and successful application throughout the study.

Perfect agreement on task paradigm description (C16-C19). Both evaluations accept these claims without challenge. Peer review demonstrates understanding by accurately summarizing the task, while OpenEval emphasizes appropriate citations and clear illustration.

Both address minimal task-irrelevant variance in trained vanilla RNNs (C68). OpenEval finds this supported by lesion analysis, explaining why PEV-based index works reliably. Peer review acknowledges this as a limitation for generalization to neural recordings (C69-C70), rating as UNCERTAIN.

Partial overlap on limitations and future applications. OpenEval rates C64, C66, C69-C70 as UNCERTAIN (speculative predictions). Peer review explicitly acknowledges the limitation that results might not generalize to neural recordings with task-irrelevant variance (C69-C70), also rating as UNCERTAIN.

Both address speculative claims about broader implications (C64, C66). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN (untested predictions), while peer review finds them SUPPORTED as reasonable extensions. Peer review notes potential interest to broad audience, implicitly supporting applicability claims.

Partial overlap on claims about extra dimensions and complex computations (C65, C67). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by citations and rank-1 model results. Peer review groups these with broader speculation claims (C64, C66) and finds them SUPPORTED as reasonable extensions.

OpenEval addresses mechanistic explanation for counterintuitive observation (C20) that both modulation types produce similar neural activity patterns. This specific claim is not explicitly evaluated separately in peer review, though it relates to findings discussed in other peer results.

Minor overlap on claims about irrelevant information persistence (C29-C30) and indistinguishability (C39-C40). OpenEval includes C29-C30 with rank-1 model findings and C39-C40 with rank-3 findings. Peer review groups these with broader framework claims about differentiating mechanisms being difficult.

Minor overlap on information flow claim (C41). OpenEval groups this with pathway-based analysis (C6, C42), while peer review includes it with claims about indistinguishability and difficulty of differentiating mechanisms (C29-C30, C39-C40).
